items.title: Anthropic Details How It Contains Claude Across Web, Code, and Cowork
items.summary_1line: Anthropic detailed the containment architectures it uses for Claude across its products. It argues that agent safety depends on placing deterministic limits on an agent’s filesystem, network, and execution environment...
items.editor_note: InfoQ reports Anthropic's account of the containment architecture — deterministic filesystem/network/execution limits — behind Claude's agent safety across web, Code, and Cowork.

editorial.tldr: Anthropic's own teams spent early July showing how they use Claude Cowork — marketing operations automating reporting and campaign builds, then guidance on pairing it with Claude Fable 5 for long, complex work. By Jul 22, Anthropic moved from use-case show-and-tell to disclosing the containment architecture underneath.
editorial.whats_new: Anthropic detailed for the first time how it technically contains Claude across Cowork, Code, and web — arguing agent safety depends on deterministic filesystem, network, and execution limits, not model judgment alone.
editorial.why_it_matters: Cowork is Anthropic's async, hand-off-and-walk-away agent product — this containment-architecture disclosure is the first concrete answer to the platform-engineer question of what actually stops an unsupervised agent from doing damage while you're away.
editorial.take_for_builders: Before handing Cowork an unattended, multi-step task, check what filesystem, network, and execution limits Anthropic actually enforces by default versus what you need to configure yourself.

status.state: Expanding · usage patterns, use cases, and containment architecture disclosed
status.detail: A week of use-case posts (marketing-ops automation, pairing with Claude Fable 5) preceded Jul 22's first detailed look at the containment architecture — filesystem, network, and execution limits — that Anthropic says agent safety depends on. No further update since.

beats.headline: Anthropic details the containment architecture behind Claude's agent safety
beats.summary: InfoQ reports Anthropic's account of how it places deterministic limits on Claude's filesystem, network, and execution environment across web, Code, and Cowork — a technical answer to what actually contains an unsupervised agent.

open_questions: What specific containment mechanisms — sandboxing, permission scopes, network egress rules — does Anthropic enforce by default in Cowork, versus what's opt-in?
Does the containment architecture change how much unattended, multi-step work a team can safely hand to Cowork, or is it primarily a trust-building message?
Do Claude Code and the web app share the same containment primitives Anthropic describes for Cowork, or does each surface implement its own limits?
